I've added the feature flag, and the notifier's 3 tests pass. One thing is missing before you can turn it on: **the new receipt template doesn't exist yet.** There's no `services/notifier/templates/` directory, and `render()` in `notifier/render.py` is still a stub that just raises an error. If you turn the flag on now, the code will ask for a template called `receipt_v2` that isn't there.

**What changed**
- `services/notifier/notifier/email.py`: `send_receipt` now uses the `receipt_v2` template when the environment variable `NOTIFIER_FF_RECEIPT_V2` is set to `"1"`. Otherwise it uses the existing `receipt` template. The notifier is deployed on its own and can't read the root `flags.toml` or `flags.is_on()`, so it uses its own environment-variable flags. The subject line and arguments are unchanged.
- `services/notifier/tests/test_email.py`: the existing test now makes sure the flag is unset. I added two tests: flag on uses `receipt_v2`, and any value other than `"1"` (e.g. `"true"`) keeps the old template.

**Still to do**
- Add `templates/receipt_v2.mjml` and a plain-text version `templates/receipt_v2.txt` using the same variables (`invoice_id`, `total_minor`), and implement `render()`. Template and copy changes are signed off in #growth-eng.
- **How gradual the rollout can be:** this flag is either on or off for a whole deployment, so you can roll out one environment at a time (staging, then prod) but not to a percentage of customers. If you want a percentage split, I can add a check based on the invoice id, but that would be a new pattern for this service, so I held off.

Nothing is committed yet.
